voice_name: Serhii Plokhy (implied by byline context; article signed by historian)
voice_affiliation: War on the Rocks / Harvard University (historian)
key_quote: A war between Russia and Ukraine, which, according to Western assessments, was quite imminent, seemed as yet uncertain here, too awful to contemplate. But its hazy presence was felt in Moscow on that murky evening: enough of a presence to concentrate minds.
key_quote_en: A war between Russia and Ukraine, which, according to Western assessments, was quite imminent, seemed as yet uncertain here, too awful to contemplate. But its hazy presence was felt in Moscow on that murky evening: enough of a presence to concentrate minds.
summary: Historian Serhii Plokhy, writing from Moscow on 2022-02-22, acknowledges Western assessments of imminent war as plausible but notes deep uncertainty in Moscow itself; he frames Putin's strategy through historical parallels to Stalin and Khrushchev's brinksmanship, suggesting risk-taking is possible but scope and timing remain unclear.

title: Trois scénarios pour la Russie en Ukraine
key_quote: La Russie vient de franchir son Rubicon : ses troupes sont désormais officiellement présentes dans l'est du territoire ukrainien... Désormais, le pouvoir russe a trois options très différentes devant lui : un scénario « géorgien »... un scénario révisionniste et maximaliste d'invasion de l'Ukraine... un scénario « azovien ».
key_quote_en: Russia has crossed its Rubicon: its troops are now officially present in eastern Ukrainian territory... Now Russian power has three very different options before it: a 'Georgian' scenario... a revisionist and maximalist scenario of invading Ukraine... an 'Azovian' scenario.
summary: The author analyzes three possible Russian military scenarios in Ukraine (limited recognition, full invasion, or limited territorial conquest), presenting invasion as plausible but contingent on Western sanctions severity, with the most likely outcome being either maximal conquest or limited territorial gains.
